analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (date bump at line 3; line 140 now cites CoordinatorReconnectPolicy instead of ExponentialBackoff in CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (date bump; new 'Close codes and the reconnect wait' section, head lines ~173-190). No code, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption behavior changes, so no regression against the threat model assets or boundaries (TB-002 provider WebSocket, TB-011 App Attest authorization) is evident.

The new section documents that the provider reads only the WebSocket close code from the coordinator side. Close 1012 gets a randomized delay without backoff growth. Any other code, or no close frame, gets the grown exponential backoff. A session that stays open for stableSessionDuration resets the backoff, and every reconnect sends a fresh register. This is consistent with the documented fresh-nonce and re-register model (T-053: stale authorization must not survive a connection change) and does not claim that reconnect grants trust or authorization. One availability-related note: a coordinator-side or on-path party sending 1012 could influence provider reconnect timing, but the coordinator is trusted, and TLS is assumed on the connection. This is an existing design point, not introduced here.

The doc claims about CoordinatorReconnectPolicy, serviceRestartDelayRange and stableSessionDuration refer to Swift sources that are not supplied in this batch. Whether the code matches the documentation (for example, that a 1012 close does not bypass the fresh-register or authorization re-evaluation path) is an unverified contract. That is a documentation-accuracy matter, not evidence of a vulnerability. The earlier troubleshooting text is unchanged elsewhere. Nothing in the diff weakens the threat-model mitigations.
